why: Route parameters and the request path travel from the document to the client
bundle through one element. Three writers emit it — the dev server's
client_hydration_script, the CLI's prerender writer, and the CSR shell — and
two generated preludes read it, one per module graph. All five have to agree
on the element and its key names or hydration silently starts with empty
It is a data block rather than an executable script on purpose. Every page
carried an inline <script> that assigned these globals, so a
Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-inline' blocked it and hydration
never started. A CSP hash could not cover it either, because the parameters
differ per request. type="application/json" is not executed, so script-src
does not apply to it at all and a strict policy needs no nonce for it.
The block is raw text inside a script element, and the parameters come
from the request URL. serde_json escapes quotes and backslashes but leaves
< alone, so a path segment containing </script> closed the element and ran
whatever followed. The CSR shell interpolated serialized JSON directly and
was reachable that way; the other two writers already escaped.
